label: DATING AGAIN

cover.headline: 4 first messages that *actually start a conversation*

points.heading: Comment on something specific
points.body: Their profile gives you an easy opening.
points.panel: “Your hiking photo looks amazing. Where was that?”

points.heading: Ask an easy, fun question
points.body: Light questions are easier to answer than “how are you?”
points.panel: “Okay, important: best snack for a road trip?”

points.heading: Share a little about you
points.body: A two-way conversation feels more natural.
points.panel: “I just tried a new coffee place. Do you have a favorite?”

points.heading: Keep it short
points.body: A short, warm message is easier to reply to.
points.panel: Two sentences, one question. That’s enough.

resource.name: Text Chemistry
resource.covers: Ideas for texting with more confidence while you’re getting to know someone.

caption:
The first message can feel like the hardest part of online dating. “Hey” rarely starts anything.

These four approaches make it easier to start real conversations. If you’d like more ideas for texting with confidence while you get to know someone, there’s a resource at the link in bio. It’s a place to start, and no resource can promise how someone will respond.
